title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Midland, TX: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Permian pipeline, gas plant and tank battery inspectors: API 1104 or ASME for Part C, Part B travel, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Midland: Six Days for Permian Basin Pipeline, Gas Plant and Tank Battery Inspectors
html:
Drive out of Midland on almost any farm-to-market road and welded steel is everywhere: gathering lines, compressor stations, gas processing plants, central tank batteries, meter runs and the large-diameter takeaway pipelines that carry Permian gas and crude toward the Gulf Coast. Somebody has to judge those welds before they are buried, coated or pressurized, and on most construction spreads and fabrication contracts in the basin that person is expected to hold the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential. Midland is also a headquarters town. Diamondback Energy, one of the largest producers in the basin, is based here, and the operators, midstream companies and contractors who build for them keep inspection crews moving across Midland, Ector, Martin and Howard counties and over the state line into New Mexico.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day exam-preparation course for Permian welders, pipeline hands moving up from the line, fabrication shop QC staff, NDT technicians and engineers who intend to sit the CWI examination. The American Welding Society writes the examination, administers it and issues the certificate. Atlantis prepares candidates and plays no part in grading; AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has never seen a question from the real exam. There is no Atlantis classroom in Midland. An individual studies online at their own pace with an instructor answering questions, a contractor can bring all six days to its own yard or field office for a group, and a candidate who wants personal coaching can book the six days one-to-one, online or in person at a place agreed when booking. The day-by-day outline is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Where the Permian's welds are coming from

Takeaway capacity is the story of 2026. In May 2026 the U.S. Energy Information Administration reported that the Blackcomb Pipeline, a 365-mile line sized for 2.5 billion cubic feet of gas a day from the Waha hub to Agua Dulce, was under construction for service in the third quarter of the year, and that Energy Transfer's Hugh Brinson Pipeline would add 2.2 billion cubic feet a day in phases. An Oil & Gas Journal survey published in June 2026 listed further projects queued behind them, among them Traverse, Eiger Express and Kinder Morgan's Trident Intrastate, with in-service targets stretching into 2027 and 2028. Every one of those lines means thousands of girth welds, tie-ins at compressor and meter stations, and assemblies fabricated in shops around Midland and Odessa.

Mainline construction is the visible part. Upstream of the big pipes, producers keep adding gathering systems, central tank batteries, saltwater disposal facilities, compression and processing capacity, and each pad needs flowlines, separators, heater-treaters and tanks. The shippers named on Blackcomb included Diamondback, Marathon, Devon and Targa, which shows how many producers and processors feed the same corridor. A CWI based in Midland can spend one month on a mainline spread working to API 1104 and the next inside a gas plant expansion where the piping is built to ASME B31.3.

The codes behind a Permian weld

Which document governs a weld depends on what the steel carries and where it sits. Intrastate gas and hazardous liquid pipelines in Texas fall under the Railroad Commission, whose pipeline safety rules in 16 Texas Administrative Code Section 8.1 adopt the federal pipeline regulations, 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, by reference; those federal parts point to API 1104 for welding and weld acceptance. Interstate lines answer to PHMSA under the same federal parts. Gas transmission piping is designed to ASME B31.8 and liquid lines to ASME B31.4, and compressor station piping on a transmission system normally stays within B31.8.

Inside a gas processing plant the picture changes: process piping is usually specified to ASME B31.3, with welders and procedures qualified to ASME Section IX. Production tanks are field-erected to API 650 or shop-welded to API Specification 12F, and the structural steel for pipe racks, platforms and skid frames follows AWS D1.1. A CWI does not need to memorize every one of these, but must know which book the contract names and how to find the acceptance table in it quickly. That is exactly the skill Part C of the AWS examination tests, in one book of the candidate's choosing.

What Permian job postings ask for

Two recent listings show the range. Danos, recruiting an inspection advisor based in Midland for construction, fabrication and maintenance work across the basin, made current or previous AWS CWI certification a requirement and asked for at least ten years in quality or inspection on major oil and gas projects, with coating inspection and NDT certifications listed as preferred. A pipeline construction role advertised for Odessa wanted a valid CWI with at least five years of pipeline inspection behind it, named API 1104 and ASME B31.4 and B31.8 as the working codes, and listed API 570 and coating credentials as advantages.

The duties in both postings read like the CWI syllabus. Verify procedures and welder qualifications before work starts. Watch fit-up, preheat and root passes. Check finished welds visually against the code, raise nonconformance reports and keep the records an operator or regulator will ask for later. Around Midland the CWI is often the entry ticket, and the additional credentials decide who gets the longer contracts.

API 1104 or the ASME option for Part C

AWS lets each candidate choose the code book for Code Application, and in Midland the choice usually comes down to two. API 1104 suits people whose work is mostly on the right-of-way: mainline and lateral construction, tie-ins, repairs and the qualification tests welders take before a spread starts. The ASME option, which combines Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, suits people based in fabrication shops and gas plants, where qualification records and process piping inspection fill the day. AWS D1.1 fits inspectors at structural fabricators building racks, skid frames and platforms. Pick the book you will actually work from, because you will keep reaching for it long after the exam. Background reading: API 1104, API 1104 weld acceptance criteria, ASME B31.8 and ASME Section IX.

Day four of the course is spent inside the chosen book. For an API 1104 candidate that means drilling the acceptance limits for inadequate penetration, incomplete fusion, burn-through, slag inclusions and porosity, the essential variables that force a procedure to be requalified, and the difference between qualifying a procedure and qualifying a welder. For an ASME candidate it means moving between Section IX variables and the examination and acceptance rules of B31.3 without losing the clock.

No AWS section in Midland or Odessa

The AWS District 18 directory, which takes in Houston, San Antonio, Corpus Christi, the Sabine area, Lake Charles, El Paso, the Rio Grande Valley and two sections in northern Mexico, lists no section based in Midland or Odessa. It does list the Odessa College student chapter, attached to the San Antonio Section. The nearest full sections on that directory are El Paso, roughly 300 miles west, and San Antonio. For a Permian inspector the professional network is therefore built mostly on the job; anyone who wants section meetings, scholarships or technical talks should use the AWS section finder on aws.org, join the section that suits them and take part remotely where possible.

Learning to weld in Midland and Odessa

Both local colleges run welding programs that feed the oil patch. Midland College, on its main campus on North Garfield, offers a welding technology Associate of Applied Science and shorter certificates. Its program covers shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, gas tungsten arc and flux cored welding in all positions on carbon and stainless steel plate and pipe, along with blueprint reading, metallurgy and layout. Odessa College offers an Associate of Applied Science in Welding and a General Welder Level 1 Certificate, its program page lists inspection and quality control among the topics, and its continuing education arm advertises preparation for the AWS inspector and educator credentials.

A degree changes the experience arithmetic. The AWS table lists two years of welding-related work for an associate degree in welding or engineering fields, against five years for a high school diploma and four for completed trade courses, and AWS decides how a particular program is classed. Graduates who go straight to the field should keep a record of every employer and job from the first day, because that history becomes the experience verification AWS asks for.

Taking the exam from West Texas

The examination has three parts and AWS requires at least 72 percent on each. Part A, Fundamentals, and Part C, Code Application, are computer-based tests booked at a Prometric test center with the eligibility code AWS sends once it accepts the application; Prometric's locator shows the nearest centers. Part B, the practical, works differently. AWS gives it where it holds its CWI seminars, typically on the weekend after a seminar week, and the AWS training locations page in November 2026 listed six Texas cities: Austin, Beaumont, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio. None of them is in West Texas, so a Midland candidate should budget for a long drive or a flight for the practical and plan it around a hitch.

Studying around hitches and long drives

Permian schedules are hard on anything fixed. Field inspectors work rotations, yard staff work long days and everybody drives. The online format exists for that: the six-day outline becomes a study plan you work through at your own pace, with course notes, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and you message an instructor whenever something will not come clear. A workable pattern for a rotational worker is to use days off for the heavier material, such as metallurgy, fabrication math and welding symbols, and keep code book drills for evenings on hitch, when a laptop and the tabbed book are all you need.

Between study blocks, the free NDT practice tests help with the nondestructive testing questions in Part A, and the Practical NDT welding workshop lets you rehearse visual inspection steps in a browser. The article on CWI results by exam part shows where candidates commonly lose marks.

Six days at a Midland or Odessa yard

For a fabricator, pipeline contractor or inspection company with several people heading for the CWI, the corporate format brings the six days to its own premises, and that pays off in the Permian. The practical day can use real coupons and cut-outs from the yard, the company's own fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges and hi-lo gauges, and the procedure and welder qualification records the crew actually works to. Day four can be built around API 1104 for a pipeline group or the ASME option for a shop that builds code piping and skids. The employer picks the weeks, which usually means between projects rather than in the middle of a spread.

Every person in the group still applies to AWS individually, meets the eligibility and vision rules personally and sits each part on their own account; the application, the vision examination and the experience verification belong to the candidate even when the employer pays the fees. For wider on-site NDT training see corporate NDT training for Midland employers.

Experience records for oilfield hands

AWS weighs education against years of welding-related work: one year with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, two with a qualifying associate degree, three with engineering or technical courses that count toward a welding bachelor's, four with completed trade or vocational courses, five with a high school diploma or equivalent, nine with eighth-grade schooling and twelve with less. The work has to be verifiable, and AWS decides what counts.

Oilfield careers create a particular problem, because many people have worked for a string of contractors on short jobs, and some of those companies no longer exist. Start collecting the evidence early. List each employer with dates, the type of work (pipeline construction, station fabrication, tank erection, repair), the processes you welded or inspected and the code the job was built to, and find a supervisor or client representative who can confirm it. A pipeliner who moved from helper to welder to welder foreman should describe each step, since duties close to inspection, such as checking fit-up or keeping weld maps, strengthen the record.

Vision is assessed separately on the AWS visual acuity form: near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with correction if you need it, plus a color perception test, carried out by a qualified eye-care or medical professional. AWS limits how old that examination may be when you sit, so book it close to your exam window. The CWI requirements guide covers the rules in more depth.

After the CWI in the Permian

A new CWI in Midland usually starts as a construction or fabrication inspector, and the next credential depends on the direction. Pipeline inspectors often add coating inspection and NDT method certifications, because owners value an inspector who can also check a coating or run a thickness survey. Inspectors heading toward operating plants look at API 570 for piping. Anyone who wants to perform testing needs method training and certification by the employer under its written practice. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training for that, for example UT Level 1 for thickness work and MT Level 2 for crack detection on welds, and the employer certifies the technician afterwards.

The CWI itself runs on a nine-year cycle, with renewal paperwork at the third and sixth years and a current vision record on file, and the Senior CWI pathway opens later for inspectors who run programs. Local pages: ultrasonic testing in Midland, magnetic particle inspection in Midland, third-party inspection in Midland, NDT training in the Permian Basin and NDT training in Odessa.

What to send for a Midland quote

Tell us whether the course is for one person or a group, which format you want, the code book you plan to use for Part C and roughly when you intend to test. For an on-site group, add the yard or office location and the weeks that avoid project peaks. If you are unsure whether your experience qualifies, summarize it in a few lines and we will point out the questions to raise with AWS before you start studying. Fees are quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Midland or Odessa?
faq.a: Not on the AWS District 18 directory, which lists no section based in either city. It lists the Odessa College student chapter under the San Antonio Section, and the nearest full sections are El Paso and San Antonio. Use the section finder on aws.org to join one.

faq.q: Should a Permian pipeline inspector choose API 1104 for Part C?
faq.a: Usually, if most of your work is mainline, lateral or repair welding on the right-of-way. Inspectors based in gas plants or code piping shops are often better served by the ASME option, and structural fabricators by AWS D1.1. Choose the book you will use at work.

faq.q: Where would a Midland candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At one of the locations where AWS holds its CWI seminars. In November 2026 the Texas cities on the AWS training locations page were Austin, Beaumont, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio, so plan travel. Parts A and C are taken at a Prometric test center.

faq.q: Can I prepare while working a rotation?
faq.a: Yes. The online format follows the six-day outline as a study plan at your own pace, and an instructor answers questions as you work. Many rotational workers do the heavier reading on days off and code book drills on hitch.

faq.q: Do Texas pipeline rules require a CWI?
faq.a: The Railroad Commission's rules adopt 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, which point to API 1104 for welding and weld acceptance. Whether an inspector must hold the CWI is usually set by the operator's specifications and the contract, and many Permian postings make it mandatory.

faq.q: I have a welding degree from Midland College. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: AWS lists two years of welding-related experience for a qualifying associate degree, compared with five for a high school diploma. AWS decides how a specific program is classed, so confirm before you apply, and keep records of every job from the start.

faq.q: Can our company host the course at its Odessa yard?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your premises for a group, using your own gauges, weld samples and qualification records. Each person still applies to AWS individually and must meet the eligibility and vision rules personally.

faq.q: Will the course make me a Certified Welding Inspector?
faq.a: No. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification. The course prepares you for Parts A, B and C; you still apply to AWS, pass the vision test and pass each part. Atlantis has no access to exam content.

faq.q: What can I add after the CWI to win longer contracts?
faq.a: Coating inspection, NDT method certification and, for plant work, API 570 are common next steps. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; see NDT training in Midland. The employer certifies the technician under its written practice.

faq.q: How do I get a quote?
faq.a: Send the format, headcount, Part C code book and your rough exam timing through the Midland enquiry form. Fees are quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.
